chunks: Al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ḥammād, from Ḥarīz, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who prayed two rakʿahs and does not know whether they are two or four. He said: “He gives salām, then stands and prays two rakʿahs with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, recites the tashahhud, and departs, and there is nothing upon him.”

key_terms.بِفَاتِحَةِ الْكِتَابِ: with Sūrat al-Fātiḥah recited in the compensatory prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two units of salat under discussion in the ruling
key_terms.فَلَا يَدْرِي: he is uncertain and does not know
key_terms.وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: no further duty or penalty remains upon him
key_terms.يُسَلِّمُ: he concludes the prayer with salām

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if he doubts whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or four in salat?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who doubts in salat whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or four. The Imam عليه السلام instructs him to complete the prayer with salām, then perform two rakʿahs with Fātiḥat al-Kitāb, after which no further liability remains upon him.
